hardest_target_inspection.limitation: The planning ledger's richer Z called for an angle slider with a live overlap gauge plus a second fixed-theta case that varies a non-overlap energy contribution. The frozen page instead uses three discrete reveal stages and prose/counterexample reasoning. It is meaningful, but it does not let the learner manipulate theta continuously or observe the underdetermination through a controlled two-variable probe.

builder_proposal.purpose: Let a learner manipulate a parameter in a declared model, observe only the quantity that model defines, then test whether a stronger system-level claim is warranted.
builder_proposal.insertion: Use the existing Core1A INTERACTIVE_BRIDGE/teaching component path; keep Shared/tools/render_core.py as the sole page renderer and retain the staged visual as the non-interactive fallback.

minimal_schema.relation_ref: canonical relation id whose meaning/conditions define the computed quantity
minimal_schema.displayed_quantity: the exact model quantity, e.g. overlap factor; never infer another quantity implicitly
minimal_schema.claim_cards: learner-classified claims tagged MODEL_DEFINED or NEEDS_ADDITIONAL_MODEL_EVIDENCE
minimal_schema.counterfactual: optional held-parameter probe that varies an explicitly non-modelled contribution
minimal_schema.reveal_policy: protect the decisive scope judgement before learner commit
minimal_schema.fallback_text: complete keyboard/screen-reader equivalent and static worked fallback

required_checks: relation_ref resolves and the displayed output label matches the relation meaning
no system-level quantity is computed unless a separate explicit relation defines it
protected conclusion is absent from pre-attempt state
keyboard, touch and screen-reader operation are equivalent
counterfactual distinguishes held variables from varied external contributions
static fallback preserves the same conceptual job without a second renderer
builder_proposal.benefit: Q9 would move from telling the fixed-theta counterexample in prose to letting the learner see why the overlap variable is insufficient; the same component generalises to model-scope questions in Chemistry and Physics.
builder_proposal.tradeoff: Adds a constrained client-side interaction and browser-test burden. The evaluator must remain declarative and relation-bound so the UI cannot accidentally imply that a simplified model is a complete physical law.
builder_proposal.migration: Opt-in only. Existing staged visuals and records remain valid; no bulk rewrite and no new production HTML renderer.
